page: Microsoft Azure F32amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor operating at 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with 3780 GB of capacity, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results place the single-core CPU performance of the AMD EPYC processor in the top 10% tier via stress-ng, while multi-core performance ranks in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently register in the top 25% tier. In database-specific benchmarks, the server achieves top 10% tier performance in PassMark database operations and top 25% in Redis SET operations. For language model workloads, the instance achieves top 10% tier performance in text generation for small (135M) and medium (7B) models, though performance drops to the middle 50% average tier when processing larger 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio combined with substantial bundled local storage offers a dense resource profile for memory-bound workloads without requiring separate storage attachments. The server is suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data processing, web serving, and moderate-sized machine learning inference tasks.
